writeup.headline: Cinemark rates Buy on strong share-price trend and a sharp revenue rebound, with half the picture missing.
writeup.thesis: Cinemark scores 73, a Buy, carried by three of six factors: growth, trend and news risk. Trend is strongest at 94: the price is 25.3% above its 200-day average, the shares are up 43.1% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, and they are 26.2 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, sitting just 2.8% below the 52-week high. Growth scores 71 on latest-quarter revenue growth of 18.9% year on year, with growth sped up by 23.6 pp from the previous quarter, though TTM revenue growth of 6.8% is more modest. News risk is a neutral-to-mildly-positive 54, helped by several analyst price-target increases ahead of the November 3 Q3 report. Quality, balance sheet and valuation could not be scored, so the rating rests on momentum and recent growth rather than on profitability or price.
key_risks: The stock looks expensive against its own history, more expensive than at 50 of the last 61 month-ends on P/S.
Results depend on the studio release slate, so one strong quarter may not repeat.
A reported Disney-backed Imax competitor could pressure premium-format pricing.
After a large run-up, the November 3 Q3 report could trigger a pullback if it disappoints.
Balance-sheet strength and margins are not reflected in the score, and cash looks small relative to debt.
what_would_change: A drop of 9 points would cut the rating to Hold, for example if the trend score fell sharply after a price pullback.
Seven more points would lift it to Strong Buy, which would need faster TTM growth or more positive news such as raised guidance.
A weak Q3 report on November 3 or negative guidance would hit both the growth and news risk scores.
